title: Are you too smart to lift?
summary: Long philosophical essay against men who think they are too smart to lift, built around an anti-bodybuilding tweet, an anti-muscle comic and an Ethan Klein clip. He blames mind-body dualism, argues physical and mental stamina are separate and boost each other's recovery, traces anti-fitness attitudes to resentment and pseudo-intellectual vanity, and attacks French mediocrity.
claims: Men who claim to be too smart to lift are, in his view, responsible for humanity's slow regression into mediocrity
People who have never pushed themselves physically cannot value training, which is why they rank memorizing fun facts above building the body
Mind-body dualism, promoted by schools and inherited from Christianity's view of the body as impure, leads people to develop the intellect and neglect the body
In school he had 2 hours of PE a week versus about 30 hours sitting in a chair
Modern post-physical society needs desk workers, so education trains mental endurance and ignores the body
Even with a desk job in AI he trains rigorously because the job does not give his body what it needs to stay healthy
Only sitting and never being active leads to atrophy and early death; we built machines to work for us and our own body-machine breaks down sooner
A mind stuck in an inactive body withers because it is disconnected from physical reality, which hurts reasoning itself
Greek philosophers trained and walked daily; Plato's name meant broad shoulders and Nietzsche walked for hours despite illness because his best ideas came while active
Socrates: no man has the right to be an amateur in physical training, meaning neglecting the body ignores half of what you are
The RPG approach of putting all stat points in intellect fails because humans have separate physical and mental stamina; unused physical stamina is simply wasted

Training the body lets mental stamina recover faster (like meditation) and reading lets physical stamina recover, so 5 hours of intellectual work plus 2 hours of training beats 7 hours of intellectual work
Our culture's image of aliens (big heads, tiny bodies, telekinesis) shows we assume advancement means abandoning the body, a path he rejects
We live in a physical world with danger; neglecting the body leaves the mind undefended
Anti-fitness men are driven by resentment: they feel physically inferior and compensate by claiming intellectual superiority instead of fixing the inferiority
As a kid he was intellectual but a skinny, weak wimp who looked down on athletic boys; being bullied taught him he had to toughen up
Making weakness your identity and hiding in escapist hobbies (card games, video games) makes the body wither and you even more of a victim
Both too much violence and never being exposed to it can produce men who flee the physical
A man needs strength to stay mentally healthy; a weak man comes to resent his own existence
Facing a stronger man, the only real fix for inferiority is to become stronger, not to convince yourself he is the idiot
He judges that weak men create weak art and that Hollywood, run by weak men, now makes strong men the butt of jokes, which young men must reject
Appearance largely reflects the mind because it results from life choices; through history muscles were associated with leadership and virtue
Women like muscles because they signal hard work, resilience, consistency and the ability to protect
Pseudo-intellectuals care about looking smart rather than being smart: signs include announcing IQ, broadcasting classical music taste and Rick and Morty shirts
People who say they could train if they wanted or looked like you at your age are talking to themselves to feel better
Men who reject training and real intellectual effort usually spend their time as passive consumers, avoiding pain and effort
French men are the best at mediocrity; the word gonflette (muscles full of air) exists only to mock people who lift
Any hobby that fulfills you and makes you progress is not a waste of time; waste of time is what keeps you stagnant or regressing
Fitness lengthens life, improves health, mood and willpower, and is the most important thing a man can do, more objectively beneficial than chess or languages
Bodybuilders must lead a cultural battle to reclaim physical values against those who say exercise is a waste of time
Training teaches discipline and protects you from becoming a hedonistic degenerate who only chases pleasure
